data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["Biological species evolve naturally; software dependencies are often chosen for efficiency/standardization, increasing correlation."],"overturn_conditions":["If the 'colony' consists of clones of the same species."],"shared_structure":["Specialized organism vs. multi-species colony","Singular immune system vs. distributed ecological resilience"],"source_memory_refs":["SCR_001"],"transfer_claims":["The 'colony' (decentralized network) survives a plague (specific bug) that kills the 'organism' (centralized service), but is vulnerable to environmental shifts (infrastructure-wide outages)."]},"claim":"A decentralized network is more resilient to correlated failure only if its heterogeneity exceeds the 'dependency threshold' of the centralized service's redundancy.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The decentralized services converge on a single industry-standard dependency (e.g., OpenSSL, as suggested in SCR_002), creating a hidden shared cause.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The cost of coordination in a decentralized network leads to consensus collapse during a crisis (SCR_004).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The centralized service implements true multi-stack heterogeneity (multi-cloud/multi-OS) that mimics decentralization (SRC_008).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Resilience is not a function of the number of nodes (redundancy) but of the diversity of failure domains. A centralized service with high redundancy often shares a single control plane or kernel (common-mode failure). A decentralized network breaks this correlation provided the services do not converge on a shared 'invisible' dependency (e.g., a specific library or cloud provider), effectively shifting the failure mode from 'systemic collapse' to 'partial degradation'.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
